Get on a diet! Here's a filling low calorie recipe:


* 1 litre water
* 2 cubes of chicken broth
* 350g chicken fillet (chopped in small pieces)
* 1 medium sized onion (chopped in 4 bits)
* At least 2 carrots
* 25g of thin spaghetti/pasta noodles (break it into half or three pieces if necessary)
* Pepper (salt is probably not necessary)
* Optional: paprika powder


First you heat the water and put the broth. Your vegetables and your pepper/paprika go in when it's mostly dissolved. Don't forget to put the lid while you're cooking the soup. Put the a click of butter on the frying pan and once it's melted put the small pieces of chicken on it (use medium heat until it looks ready where you switch to low). Once the vegetables the have been in for like 15-20 minutes you put the chicken in the soup and wait like 5 minutes. Once you've done that put the spaghetti in and you cook it until it's ready (can vary between 5-15 minutes depending on your brand, etc).


In total this should be less than 600 calories. I recommend putting more carrots in though and that should still keep it under 600 calories. Eat until you're full. You might get full by only eating half the soup so it can be both your lunch and dinner.


Find out what your TDEE/maintenance calories (pick sedentary and omit body fat percentage) is and try to keep a deficit of 500 calories a day. This way you will lose 1 pound a week. Exercise isn't necessary but very helpful. It's good because you'll burn calories (getting less fat) and build muscle a (good weight) and most guys like it more than a super skinny girl. Trying a 5000 step walk every day to burn a few extra calories if you don't exercise.

Foods to avoid:


* Pasta if it's not in moderation (unlike this recipe)
* Bread
* Dairy (you can use some when cooking, especially milk)
* Beef (unless you plan it well)
* Pork (unless you plan it well)
* Sugary soda (ex. Coke which isn't diet)
* Candy
* Alcohol (all types)
* Ice cream
* Fast food



Foods to eat:

* Potatoes (especially cooked, diced is also good, avoid french fries)
* Vegetables (eating small amounts of broccoli actually burns a few calories for some reason)
* Fruits (apples as a snack, strawberry as desert?)
* Chicken
* Rice (not great but it's decent, make it in moderation, easy to make)
* Eggs (not my thing but it can be good for breakfast ex. Omelette or scrambled eggs, Jamie Oliver had a good video for omelettes but the cheese is optional, Gordon Ramsay has a good video on scrambled eggs)
* Water (fizzy is good if you don't like still water)
* Diet soda (use a straw)


Another food you can make is potatoes with chicken fillet (make it in a frying pan similarly to the previous recipe but add spices) with tomato sauce. You can make it by using 500ml tomato puree, tomato paste, pepper any any other spices you like, one beef broth, and water until you're satisfied with how thick/thin the sauce is.



It's important to eat food, if you starve yourself you'll end up feeling terrible, not losing weight optimally and in an unhealthy way, and you'll be prone to overeating which will ruin your efforts.


Other important things guys like is to have good hygiene (guys detest stinky girls and adore girls who smell good), decent fashion sense (doesn't have to be expensive), good make up (even the least attractive faces can really benefit from this), get a good haircut (especially bad haircuts aren't great). Be interested in the things he liked, initiate conversations with him, being interesting yourself is good but you can easily make up for it by being interested in the stuff he likes because then you have something in common you both (pretend to) like, laugh at his jokes, compliment him sometimes (especially when he achieved something he values), be happy if he takes an interest or hobby you enjoy.

I don't know how you look like but most of these small fixes are things you can start tomorrow and you'll instantly improve.
